title: Study Confirms Liberals Have Fewer Kids Than Conservatives | Institute for Family Studies
gist: A June 2026 IFS report, 'The Ideological Fertility Divide,' based on a survey of more than 7,000 Americans aged 18-54, finds conservatives have 1.40 children on average versus 1.09 for liberals—28% more—with the gap attributed partly to higher parenting fears among liberals.

insights.claim: A June 2026 IFS report titled 'The Ideological Fertility Divide' finds conservative adults have 1.40 children on average versus 1.09 for liberals, meaning conservatives have 28% more children than liberals.
insights.speaker: Steven Ertelt
insights.so_what: A durable fertility gap along ideological lines compounds into diverging future population shares, with long-run political and consumer-market implications.
insights.quote: conservative adults have 1.40 children on average, compared to an average of 1.09 for liberals

insights.claim: The IFS report is based on survey results from more than 7,000 Americans aged 18-54 and finds statistically significant gaps between ideology types in both the number of children adults have and the number they want.
insights.speaker: Steven Ertelt
insights.so_what: The gap appears in both actual and desired fertility, suggesting it is preference-driven and unlikely to close through economic policy alone.
insights.quote: based on survey results from more than 7,000 Americans aged 18-54
insights.locator: Liberal Americans have and desire fewer children

insights.claim: The report attributes the ideological fertility gap at least in part to higher fears about parenting among liberals.
insights.speaker: Steven Ertelt
insights.so_what: If attitudinal fear rather than material constraint drives the gap, pro-natal subsidies would have limited effect on the more anxious cohort.
insights.quote: This gap is due, at least in part, to higher fears about parenting among liberals.
insights.locator: Liberal Americans have and desire fewer children
